rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are evidence that Joseph was innocent.
rows.anchor: The word “signs” here refer to the evidence of Joseph’s innocence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz and his relatives knew Joseph was blameless and Zelicha was entirely at fault.
rows.anchor: ‘Azīz and his relatives fully understood that he was not at fault. It was Zelicha who was entirely at fault.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid embarrassment, they proposed imprisoning Joseph for a while.
rows.anchor: to save evade embarrassment they proposed to imprison Joseph (sws) for some time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expected Zelicha's infatuation and public interest to fade, leaving people to think Joseph was guilty and punished.
rows.anchor: people too would loose interest in this whole incident.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masters had unrestricted power over enslaved people, so Aziz could readily send Joseph to prison.
rows.anchor: The masters of those times had unlimited authority over their slaves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz's government office and rank in the royal guard would have let him overcome any obstacle to imprisonment.
rows.anchor: a person like him who was a government official and also a dignitary of the royal guard would have easily overcome it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins another trial; although people might deem it the hardest, Joseph desired it because faith and character mattered most.
rows.anchor: since faith and character occupied the real importance, he actually desired in fact prayed for this scenario in contrast with the previous one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an leaves the two prisoners unidentified.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān has not revealed the identity of the two young boys.

rows.speaker: Torah
rows.claim: On the Torah's account, one youth served the king wine and the other was his baker.
rows.anchor: Torah is accepted, it seems that one of them had the duty to serve wine to the king and the other one was his baker.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their unusual dreams made them curious, and having observed Joseph's knowledge and piety, they naturally asked him to interpret them.
rows.anchor: were impressed by his knowledge and piety. Thus it was very natural that they termed to him for this interpretation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhsin describes someone who acts in everything as if standing in God's presence.
rows.anchor: someone who does everything as if he is standing in God’s presence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food distribution would briefly relieve the prison's monotonous, bleak routine, so Joseph referred to it while delaying his answer.
rows.anchor: the distribution of food would have been considered a break in such bleak routine.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prisoners would think Joseph took their dreams seriously and was not dismissing them with a casual answer.
rows.anchor: had been given importance by him and that he did not want to dismiss it by giving a casual explanation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph used the delay as an opening to preach, seeking worship of God for his companions' success in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: Joseph (sws) created for himself a window of opportunity from this delay to preach the truth to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not claim dream interpretation as his own source of knowledge; he identified it as a gift from God.
rows.anchor: he himself was not the source of this knowledge; his Lord was.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph said God's blessing followed his departure from those who disbelieve in Him.
rows.anchor: this blessing of God on him was because he had left those people who did not believe in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those without belief in God reject the Hereafter, since belief in it cannot arise without belief in God.
rows.anchor: such people who reject the hereafter because the question of this belief cannot even arise for those who do not believe in God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sowed the basic teachings of religion in their hearts and indicated that embracing them required leaving disbelief in God and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: he sowed the seeds of all the basic teachings of religion in their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He indicated that adopting this path requires courage to leave the ways of disbelievers in God and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they will have to leave the ways of those who do not believe in God and in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph accepted truth after evaluating it, not merely by inheritance, and rejected falsehood because its falsity was evident.
rows.anchor: it was not merely because he had inherited it from his forefathers but because it was worthy of acceptance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rejection of disbelief and the Hereafter reflects deliberate judgment that falsehood was clear to him.
rows.anchor: he had fully evaluated truth and falsehood in his mind and was convinced on them as a result of this contemplation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph explained the faith he adopted so his companions would not mistake it for a path of his own invention.
rows.anchor: He deemed this explanation to be necessary so that the two young individuals were not under the misconception

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph links his faith to the renowned line of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, whose names may have been known to the prisoners.
rows.anchor: Their names were well known in nearby lands and it may well be that these two jail companions of Joseph (sws) were also aware of them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism is naturally and logically superior, and its prior historical importance is also established.
rows.anchor: natural and logical superiority of the religion of monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One Creator made the world, sustains its inhabitants, and alone controls life and death; there is no evidence for partners in these acts.
rows.anchor: a single creator has brought this world into existence; it is He Who has given life and sustenance to everyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without evidence in reason, nature, or the inner and outer world, people have no right to associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: what right have they to associate partners with Him without any grounds?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's warm address draws on shared hardship, which can create sympathy, sincerity, and mutual kindness and direct listeners to his goodwill.
rows.anchor: At times, facing the same hardship induces the sentiments of sympathy, love, sincerity and mutual consideration and kindness to a great degreee.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qahhar means the One who controls and dominates everyone, with none outside His jurisdiction.
rows.anchor: means one who controls and dominates everyone; none is beyond his jurisdiction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is self-evident to monotheists and polytheists alike, but claims that He has associates need strong proof.
rows.anchor: He is a self-evident reality – in fact, the most self-evident of realities and both polytheists and monotheists believe in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With no proof for divine associates, making beings gods out of desire is irrational; human nature prefers one master to many.
rows.anchor: If a slave is asked whether he likes having one master or several, he will definitely prefer the first option.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have no natural wish to submit to extra gods; belief in one God follows reason and nature, so the burden is to explain associating others.
rows.anchor: A human being’s nature is no different. He has no interest to make someone god and make him dominate his affairs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's parable contrasts a slave with many masters and conflicting aims with one owned by a single master, illustrating human nature.
rows.anchor: slave who has many masters having different objectives and another slave who is in the total ownership of one master.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God's domination follows from His attributes, there is no need to associate others in His godhead.
rows.anchor: when God dominates and controls all and this is also the essential consequence of His attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets seize opportunities to invite people to God's message; Joseph preached monotheism before interpreting the prisoners' dreams.
rows.anchor: he first delivered the message of monotheism to them and after that intepreted their dream for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The master Joseph asked the freed prisoner to mention him to was the king, whose wine-server was that prisoner.
rows.anchor: The word “master” here refers to the king and this person was the wine-server of the king.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Joseph means conveying his knowledge and wisdom, especially his skill in interpreting dreams, to the king.
rows.anchor: The word “mention” here means to convey Joseph’s knowledge and wisdom that came to his observation, in particular, his dream interpretation skill.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph saw the request as a possible way out after all routes to justice had closed.
rows.anchor: a way out for him in a situation where all doors to justice had been closed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a legitimate plan for a legitimate aim is compatible with trust in God; resorting to illegitimate means after frustration is not.
rows.anchor: Planning a legitimate scheme to achieve a legitimate purpose is not against trust in God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True reliance includes effort with available means while respecting God's limits, rather than doing nothing and merely trusting.
rows.anchor: uses all means and resources but at every step respects the boundaries set by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This disciplined effort under hardship is the test and purpose for which God created the world.
rows.anchor: This is the real test for which God has created this world and it is actually the very purpose of its creation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation (iḍāfat) in the relevant expression follows the same grammatical pattern as another cited construction.
rows.anchor: nature of annexure ( iḍāfat)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The freed prisoner forgot Joseph's request; the text attributes the forgetting to Satan because Satan makes people forget virtuous acts.
rows.anchor: This forgetfulness is asrcibed to Satan. This because it is Satan who makes people forget acts of virtue.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must plan and use means, but whether the plan succeeds depends on God's wisdom; accordingly Joseph remained imprisoned longer.
rows.anchor: the materialization of this plan depends on God’s wisdom and scheme.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's fellow prisoner forgot his request after release, fulfilling God's wise plan that Joseph stay in prison longer.
rows.anchor: it was a requisite of God’s wisdom that Joseph (sws) remain in prison for some more years.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills a plan, its means begin to arise on their own, however unlikely it may seem.
rows.anchor: its means and resources start coming into being out of their own accord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king considered his dream significant and suspected his naive courtiers could not interpret it.
rows.anchor: The king regarded this dream to be very significant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream suppresses the second half of its image: the dry ears consume the green ears, as verse 48 clarifies; the translation supplies the omission.
rows.anchor: seven dry ears were eating away the seven green ones.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍagth means a bundle of withered shrubs or vegetation; its plural can denote baseless ideas or bits of information, yielding the expression for confused dreams.
rows.anchor: means a pack of whithered shrubs and vegetation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers described such dreams as products of a gaseous stomach with no interpretive significance.
rows.anchor: They are the result of a gaseous stomach and have no significance as regards as their implication.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers tried to pacify the king and protect their reputation, claiming competence with meaningful dreams but not baseless ones.
rows.anchor: They meant that they were capable of interpreting meaningful dreams and not such baseless ones.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words rendered as remembering are synonymous.
rows.anchor: The words ذ ,  ددand ذدare synonymous.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah here means a period of time.
rows.anchor: The word #%!ٌﻣﺔ means “a period of time.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wine-server recalled Joseph's accurate interpretation of his own dream, which he had long forgotten to mention to the king.
rows.anchor: The helplessness of the courtiers in interpreting the dream reminded the wine-server of Joseph’s skill in interpreting his own dream.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He immediately offered to interpret the king's dream if allowed to visit Joseph.
rows.anchor: he could interpret this dream for them if they allow him to go and meet Joseph (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context implies the courtiers let the wine-server visit Joseph, though this step is omitted from the account.
rows.anchor: the courtiers ultimately allowed the wine-server to go to Joseph (sws) and he went to him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shows that the wine-server knew Joseph as pure and truthful through their prison experience and greatly admired him.
rows.anchor: because of his experiences in jail with him he knew that Joseph (sws) was an embodiment of purity and veracity too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He addressed Joseph as a man of his word rather than merely as a dream interpreter, an expression encompassing his noble attributes.
rows.anchor: His words were: “O man of your words” which comprehensively covers all his noble attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about people learning hints that others were guessing wildly while Joseph could interpret correctly.
rows.anchor: people are only making wild guesses in intepreting this dream.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazraʿūn is grammatically a declarative, but it functions as an imperative, a style suited to advice and guidance and paralleled elsewhere in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: occurs as an enunciative (khabar) but implies the imperative.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph supplied a practical drought strategy in addition to interpreting the dream.
rows.anchor: not only told them the interpretation of the dream but also guided them to a practical suggestion to combat the seven years of drought.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving grain in its ears protects it from termites, insects, and other damage while it is stored.
rows.anchor: as long as the corn is in the ears, they remain secure from termite, insects and other calamities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following seven years of drought destroy the stored grain, leaving very little.
rows.anchor: This drought will destroy the grain they had saved. Very little will remain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph also promised a year after the drought when God answers people's pleas, sends abundant rain, and yields a large grape harvest.
rows.anchor: He will send down abundant rain and they will get a thumping crop of grapes.

rows.speaker: Some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters understand yugāth as rain.
rows.anchor: Some people have interpreted the word #!#.ﻐﺎث as rain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal sense is seeking help, which portrays drought's full effects; rain is a consequential translation rather than the word's literal meaning.
rows.anchor: By taking the word in its literal meaning of “seeking help”, a comprehensive picture of the all-embracing affects of drought on people is portrayed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary year is one in which people cry out and plead with God until their pleas are answered.
rows.anchor: people will cry out and be forced to plead and beg the Almighty until finally their pleadings will be answered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardship drives even extreme polytheists and disbelievers to call on the one God and forget their imagined deities, as the Qur'an says.
rows.anchor: the most extreme polytheists and disbelievers cry out for help from the one God and forget their hypothetical deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph guided Egypt through the drought, winning the admiration of everyone from the king to ordinary people.
rows.anchor: This period of drought was passed by the people of Egypt under the guidance of Joseph (sws). This made everyone from the king to the masses his great admirers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿṣirūn also has a consequential sense of abundant rain and productive grape vines; mentioning grape pressing subtly suits the king's wine-server.
rows.anchor: The creepers of grapes will become very productive. People will profusely squeeze grapes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context implies the messenger reported Joseph's interpretation to the king, who was impressed and immediately summoned him; the narrative omits these steps.
rows.anchor: made the request stated in the verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger would expect a prisoner who had endured years in jail to be glad of release and leave at once.
rows.anchor: expectations made the request stated in the verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph insisted that the episode used to imprison him be investigated before he accepted release.
rows.anchor: He wanted the incident which was used as an excuse to imprison him to be investigated first.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of the conspiracy assured Joseph, while an investigation would clear him and prevent later blame.
rows.anchor: this was sufficient assurance for him that his Lord knew the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph would not accept release or closeness to the king on a temporary benefit of doubt; he prioritized clearing his name and trusted his truthfulness and God.
rows.anchor: he did not like to be freed and become closer to the king

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king summoned the women after receiving Joseph's request, and his wording shows he already believed Joseph innocent and the women deceptive.
rows.anchor: by that time he was fully sure that Joseph (sws) was innocent and these women were the deceivers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the king been unsure, he would have asked neutrally what had happened between the women and Joseph.
rows.anchor: What is the incident that took place between you and Joseph?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth becomes manifest through patience, until circumstances and even enemies testify to the truthful person's veracity.
rows.anchor: the time definitely comes when everything around him bears witness to his veracity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expressions ḥāshā and ḥāsha are used to clear someone of blame.
rows.anchor: used to absolve someone of blame.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's patience left no room for accusation, so the women openly admitted finding no evil desire in him.
rows.anchor: the women also openly confessed that they did not find any evil desire in him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of Aziz went further than the other women in confessing the truth.
rows.anchor: The wife of ‘Az īz went way ahead from these women in her confession of the truth as can be seen from her words in the verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph explained why he reopened the matter even though the king had planned to free him without investigating it.
rows.anchor: the king had made up his mind to free him without bringing it up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun meaning “that he may know” refers to the king, while the pronoun for betrayal refers to Aziz; clear context makes the apparent ambiguity no defect.
rows.anchor: for which clear concomintant indications exist.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph did not claim immunity from desire: the soul can urge sin, and people remain safe from it only through God's grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: he has these desires and his soul also induces him to sin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's safety from temptation was due to God's mercy, not an absence of desire; God forgives and shows mercy.
rows.anchor: if he was secure from trials, it was not because desires do not bother him; it was because of God’s mercy on him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase “except whom my Lord shows mercy,” the particle ma denotes a locus.
rows.anchor: the letter !ﻣﺎ is connotes a locus.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people innate awareness of virtue and vice and leaves them free to choose between them.
rows.anchor: He has innately given human beings the awareness of virtue and vice and after that they are free to choose between them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who choose virtue and endure trials steadfastly receive God's grace and are helped along the path to their destination.
rows.anchor: if a person chooses the path of virtue and faces trials with steadfastness, he receives the grace and affection of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who choose vice are given respite by God.
rows.anchor: if a person adopts the path of vice, he is given respite by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph persevered through trials, subdued base desires, and reached the high rank God ordained for him.
rows.anchor: he subdued his base desires and he was bestowed with a high rank that was ordained for him from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A new phase begins: Joseph is released and Egypt comes under his authority.
rows.anchor: Not only was he released from prison, the whole country of Egypt came under his control.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the drought Joseph fed Egypt and helped neighboring countries meet their food needs.
rows.anchor: he efficiently succeed in providing food for all the people, he was also is able to help out neighbouring contries in their edible needs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His brothers, who had caused his enslavement and imprisonment, came to obtain grain without knowing who he was.
rows.anchor: The brothers who were instrumental in having him enslaved and ultimately been thrown in prison come to his presence to obtain grain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph used his brothers' ignorance to test whether they had changed; eventually they recognized his identity and he called his parents and brothers to join him.
rows.anchor: Finally, the time came when these brothers become aware of the identity of the person to whom they had come to for the grain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the family bowed before Joseph, his earlier dream of the sun, moon, and eleven stars was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: the dream seen by Joseph (sws) comes true when he saw that the sun and the moon and eleven stars were prostrating before him.
